newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW says will seek to reverse German slide.
newsitem.headline: VW says will seek to reverse German slide.

text.p: A top executive at Volkswagen AG said on Tuesday that the German carmaker would seek to reverse its market share losses in Germany recorded in 1996 while keeping up a quick pace of international expansion.

VW management board member Robert Buechelhofer told Reuters Financial Television that the German market in 1996 was "extremely competitive" but that VW still remained the top car seller in the country.
VW said earlier on Tuesday that its German sales rose a mere 2.6 percent to 969,400 units from 944,600 in 1995 but reported double-digit global growth.
The German federal motor office at the weekend also said VW's market share fell to 19 percent in 1996 from 19.4 percent in 1995 as deliveries to customers rose 2.6 percent to 969,
"The German market is extremely competitive and we already have a high position," Buechelhofer said. "We hope we can reverse the trend in 1997."
"We will of course also try to provide the right supply for the German markets," he said. "Part of our supply in 1996 was directed into international markets."

Buechelhofer, in the interview which will be broadcast on Wednesday, said VW focused heavily on eastern Europe, Japan and North America in 1996 -- all areas that showed annual growth in vehicle deliveries of more than 20 percent.

He said vehicles from VW's Czech subsidiary Skoda were "the right product" for eastern Europe and that sales in North America were helped by product repositioning, revamped communication strategies and new dealer programmes.
"We implemented a breakthrough strategy in North America and it worked out nicely," he said, noting the carmaker would seek to keep up the pace of expansion in 1997.
In Japan, Buechelhofer said VW found success with its subcompact Polo, which was introduced into the market in mid-1996 and received aggressive marketing help.
